items.stem:
Read the following extract on national self-determination and nationalism and pluralism and answer the questions that follow.
"Tagore criticised a narrow nationalism that set people against one another. Some groups, such as the Basques in Spain and the people of Quebec in Canada, have sought greater autonomy. The demand for national self-determination has led to the formation of many new states."
(i) Accepting and accommodating different cultural groups within one state is called: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'pluralism' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Creating a separate state for every community is not practical. (2)
items.answer: (i) pluralism (ii) The acceptance and accommodation of different cultural, religious and linguistic groups within one state. (iii) Almost every state contains several cultural communities living together.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) pluralism (ii) The acceptance and accommodation of different cultural, religious and linguistic groups within one state. (iii) Almost every state contains several cultural communities living together.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"A nation is not the same as a group bound by race, religion or language alone. Members of a nation share a vision of the future and aspire to self-government. Nations are built on shared beliefs, history, territory, political ideals and identity. Nationalism helped unify Germany and Italy in the nineteenth century."
(i) Explain the term 'nationalism', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Shared history is important for a nation. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Nationalism always leads to the unification of states." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The feeling of belonging to a nation and the political doctrine that nations should have their own state. (ii) People's sense of a common past strengthens their sense of identity. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It has also led to the break-up of empires and states.
